e:
Assessment Q2. State TWO purposes of operating systems. [2 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.
Provide a user interface [1] and manage RAM/application memory [1]. Other correctly described functions: file, peripheral, user management, multitasking.

Assessment Q3. A school uses two programs simultaneously and installs a new printer. Explain how OS memory management and a device driver each help. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.
The OS allocates RAM to running programs [1], allowing each to hold working data [1]. A device driver enables OS communication with the printer [1] by providing device-specific instructions [1].

Assessment Q4. A business stores confidential records and needs to reduce the size of old backups. Explain the purposes of encryption and compression utilities. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.
Encryption converts plaintext to ciphertext [1], helping keep data unreadable without a key [1]. Compression reduces data size [1], saving storage space for backups [1].

Assessment Q5. A youth club collects personal information for event registration. Explain TWO responsibilities relating to the Data Protection Act 2018. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.

Collect only personal information necessary for a stated lawful purpose [1], avoiding irrelevant details [1]. Protect records with appropriate security/access limits [1], preventing unauthorised viewing or disclosure [1].

Assessment Q6. Evaluate a council decision to make booking local services online-only. Include a benefit, a social drawback and an environmental consideration. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.

Online bookings may be faster/more convenient [1], reducing staff administration or travel [1]. People without devices or broadband may be excluded [1], making access unfair [1]. Less paper/travel may reduce some resources [1], though servers/devices use energy and create e-waste [1]. Any balanced context-grounded evaluation accepted.

Assessment Q7. A student enters a staff account without permission and copies a paid program to distribute it. Explain the Computer Misuse Act, copyright, and one difference between open-source and proprietary licensing. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.

Unauthorised entry into computer materials may breach the Computer Misuse Act [1] even if no records are changed [1]. Copying/distributing copyrighted software without permission may infringe the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 [1] because copying rights are controlled by the rights holder/licence [1]. Open source generally gives access to code and permitted modification under conditions [1], whereas proprietary software typically restricts access/modification [1].

Assessment Q8. A school wants to create a lunchtime meal-order program. Explain how decomposition and abstraction would help its design. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.

Decomposition divides the problem into smaller tasks [1], such as reading orders, calculating totals and showing receipts [1]. This makes development/testing manageable [1]. Abstraction keeps prices, items and quantities [1], ignores irrelevant details such as dining-room wall colour [1] and therefore reduces complexity without losing essential information [1].

Assessment Q9. An algorithm calculates the cost of a cinema ticket and prints a message if the customer is aged 16 or above. Identify ONE input, ONE process, ONE output and TWO relevant flowchart-symbol roles. [5 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.

Input: customer's age or ticket price [1]. Process: calculate cost/compare age against 16 [1]. Output: ticket cost or eligibility message [1]. A decision diamond selects Yes/No branch [1]. Input/output parallelogram represents entered age or displayed result [1].

Assessment Q10. Trace: total = 3; total = total + 4; if total > 6 then print("Large") else print("Small") endif. State the two values of total, the condition result and the output. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style assessment question; not an official OCR past-paper original.
Initial total = 3 [1]; after adding 4 total = 7 [1]; 7 > 6 is true [1]; printed output is Large [1].
